subject: Follow-up: Long-context evals — models, prompts, and truncation risks
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Long-context evals — models, prompts, and truncation risks

Hi Anna / Tom,

Thanks again for taking time today — really helpful call. Below is a concise recap + proposed plan so we can move to a short pilot. I put Rishi and Monica on copy for evaluation and ops alignment.

Recap (30min call):
- Primary goal: accurate, faithful summarization of entire encounter notes (avg 8–12k tokens, some up to ~28k).
- Primary risks you flagged: truncation of important context (med history), hallucinated summaries, and edge cases at token boundaries.
- Success criteria: summary recall on a set of 50 annotated cases >= 92% on key-medication and diagnosis extraction; no high-severity hallucination on 95% of test cases.

Recommended short pilot (2 weeks):
1) Models to try (hosted + private compatibility):
   - redwood-mid-16k-int8 (good balance cost/latency; expect truncation at extremes)
   - llama-3-32k-q4 (longer context, higher GPU cost; good for fidelity)
2) Evaluation set: we propose 50 gold cases (we can redact real-case PHI or use synthetic variants) + 20 high-edge cases (very long SOAPs).
3) Prompting approach: chunk + KV-prefixing for historical meds; instructive system prompt and a two-pass summarization (extract key facts -> condensed narrative). Sample prompt set attached.
4) Monitoring & guardrails: ROUGE/QA checks + hallucination detector and automatic fallback to longer model variant when token usage > 16k.

Attachments: clinicco_call_notes.pdf (call notes), clinicco_long_context_eval_plan.xlsx (pilot plan + timeline), clinicco_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts and labeling schema).

Next steps (can we confirm by EOD Monday):
- Anna: confirm pilot scope and whether you can share sample redacted notes for the 50-case set.
- Tom: internal procurement/SSO point of contact — who owns SOC2/HIPAA review?
- Redwood: we’ll ship a configured eval harness and a short benchmark run within 48 hours of receiving samples.

Thanks — Neha

Subject: Internal: quantization / fidelity notes for ClinicCo pilot

(Internal notes — not sent to ClinicCo)

Quick notes following the call and Neha's follow-up:
- Quantization risks: int8 can introduce subtle token-level distribution shifts that sometimes surface as minor hallucinations in low-resource factual recall (med dosages). Recommend we run the fidelity QA with both float16 and int8 for the same prompt set and compare extraction metrics.
- KV cache behavior: for models with segmented KV caches, we should test prefixing vs full-chunk concatenation for meds/history; measure retrieval recall at 4k/8k/16k prefixes.
- Regression checks: produce a small set of golden QA pairs for meds/diagnoses and compute per-case divergence (answer-level F1 + a hallucination severity flag).
- Ops: instrument token usage and model-switch trigger (if token_count > 16k, auto-route to llama-3-32k with a throttled concurrency).

Action items for us: prepare two harness configs (hosted run + VPC run) and a short notebook that compares float16 vs int8 outputs on 10 canonical cases.

— Rishi
